transcript: Woman: Good morning, Riverside Community Kitchen.
Man: Hi, I would like to book the weekend bread course.
Woman: Of course. That starts on Saturday the fourteenth at nine thirty.
Man: And how much is it?
Woman: Forty-five pounds, and that includes all the flour and an apron.
Man: Great. My name is Daniel Brook.

academic.title: The return of urban bees
paragraphs: Over the last decade, rooftop beehives have appeared on offices, hotels and schools in many large cities. Supporters argue that urban hives help pollinate parks and gardens and raise awareness of declining insect numbers.

However, some ecologists warn that too many honeybee hives can harm wild bees, which compete for the same flowers. In parts of central London, the number of hives per square kilometre is now higher than in most farmland.
Researchers therefore recommend planting more flowering plants before adding new hives. A city, they say, should measure the food available to insects rather than simply count beehives.
